findings.reason: the section's whole purpose is one shared metric; the author either routes the Solov'ev certifier through the section's comparator or states in §4 why that consumer is out of scope, either of which rewrites §4 and its done-when.
findings.text: §4 states a single shared implementation for "symmetric sup and symmetric RMS nearest-polyline distances in metres", but wires only the two EFIT banks (MAST corroboration and the DIII-D match); a second symmetric nearest-polyline metric already exists at `benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py:1305` (`_symmetric_polyline_distance`, a sampled symmetric Hausdorff distance — the sup case of the same family), computing on the same polyline inputs. The stated goal of consolidation therefore forks again, and the owner to extend is `nova/equilibrium/boundary_comparison.py` (`compare_closed_boundaries` / the `_point_to_segment_distances` population).

findings.reason: the section must account for the interface surface it adds; a one-line statement of what it retires, or why nothing can be retired, is what the item requires.
findings.text: §3 introduces the exported definition `assemble_separatrix_branches` (and companions) at zero public-definition budget, and the section names no definition it retires or merges, nor states why nothing can be — in contrast to §2, which retires the local quadratic `_refine_selected_vertices` and §4, which replaces `_binding_contour` and `_separatrix`.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each contract lands behind one entry point that hides substantial behaviour: `polish_stationary_points(spline, seed_rz, valid)` (the fixed Newton kernel), `assemble_separatrix_branches(...)` (the graph assembly, split, and fixed-capacity classification), `compare_closed_boundaries(...)` (polyline sampling, nearest-segment population, sup/RMS/X metrics). One module per contract, not a fan of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4's "one shared metric implementation" in `nova/equilibrium/boundary_comparison.py` leaves a second symmetric nearest-polyline metric unretired at `benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py:1305`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 adds the public definition `assemble_separatrix_branches` without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the capability reuse map (`docs/figures/efit-baseline-demonstration/reuse-map.md`, commit `4b702960`, 25 candidates over nova and imas-ambix at pinned revisions), and every mechanism it names exists as cited: `nova.equilibrium.flux_surface_connectivity.traced_spline_contour`, `nova.equilibrium.stencil_nulls.xpoint_candidates`, `nova.equilibrium.separatrix_clip._traced_clip` / `TracedClippedSupports`, `nova.linalg.tensor_spline.fit_tensor_spline`. Re-running the search over nova I found no pre-existing closed-plus-open branch assembler, confirming the one gap the map names.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no thin layer over existing machinery is proposed; §2 factors an embedded loop into a kernel, §3 composes the existing traced-spline arcs and reuses the `TracedClippedSupports` padding/overflow conventions rather than forking them, and §4 consolidates two existing metrics rather than wrapping either twice.
